episode_title: Alyssa Aviles / Creative Growth Partner & Design Educator

real_qa.q: How did Alyssa Aviles transition from rejection by a university graphic design program to launching a successful design career?
real_qa.r: After her initial university denied her application to the graphic design program, Alyssa eventually enrolled at Valencia College, a community college that had a two-year design program. Before she even graduated, she had job offers from agencies and was already freelancing. She credits her professors and teachers at Valencia College for seeing potential in her when the other university could not, and for providing guidance and encouragement that shaped her career.
real_qa.requete: Alyssa Aviles graphic design program rejected university

real_qa.q: What is the back end of a challenge in Pedro Adeo's online marketing model and how does it generate revenue?
real_qa.r: The back end of a challenge refers to the transformation and next offer step presented after the time-based online event ends. Participants attend daily lessons over several days to build know, like, and trust with the instructor. At the end, attendees are invited to take the next step, which could be a membership, course purchase, coaching program, or other offering. Pedro Adeo made seven figures on the back end of challenges, which was completely unheard of at the time.
real_qa.requete: challenge marketing back end funnel Pedro Adeo

real_qa.q: Which high-profile entrepreneurs and personalities did Alyssa Aviles design challenge funnels for at 100X?
real_qa.r: Alyssa designed challenge funnels for Damon John from Shark Tank, Grant Cardone, Tony Robbins and Dean Graziosi together, Lisa Nichols, Les Brown, Stu McLaren, and Ryan Dice, among many others. She notes there were no other challenge funnel models to reference at the time, so she and Pedro were essentially pioneering and developing the format as they went.
real_qa.requete: Alyssa Aviles designed challenges Damon John Tony Robbins Grant Cardone

real_qa.q: How did Alyssa Aviles discover Pedro Adeo through a Facebook ad and what initial judgment did she make about his marketing funnel?
real_qa.r: Alyssa came across a Facebook ad from Pedro Adeo while doom scrolling. She researched him and discovered he had a Two Comma Club award from ClickFunnels, meaning he had made seven figures in a funnel. However, she initially judged his funnel harshly because it was a blank white page with a logo made in a brush-style font called Caveat Brush and copy in the same illegible typeface—not good for screens. Despite this initial negative impression, the copy pulled her in enough to fill out an application for his free 30-day masterclass.
real_qa.requete: Pedro Adeo Two Comma Club ClickFunnels seven figures

real_qa.q: What was the cost of Adobe Creative Suite when Alyssa Aviles taught herself graphic design as a broke college student?
real_qa.r: When Alyssa was offered the chance to learn graphic design in exchange for making posters for a faith-based organization, the Adobe Creative Suite cost approximately $700. It came on physical media with around a hundred CDs that had to be installed one at a time.

guest.bio_context: Alyssa Aviles is a multi-passionate creative with over 16 years of experience in graphic design, photography, and digital marketing. She transitioned from freelance designer and photographer to becoming a key design contractor for Pedro Adeo's 100X community, where she pioneered challenge funnel design during the early online marketing boom. She has designed marketing funnels and challenges for notable figures including Damon John from Shark Tank, Grant Cardone, Tony Robbins, Dean Graziosi, and Lisa Nichols, and has since shifted focus toward understanding marketing psychology and funnel strategy alongside design.
